title: CPC Week-2 hazard levels (CONUS, 2017-2026) matched observations only as 'at least once' for heavy rain but 'per day' for cold minima, and hit rates followed the local base rate
abstract: We tested the experimental probabilistic polygons of the NOAA CPC Week-2 (days 8-14) U.S. Hazards Outlook. Each polygon states Slight (20%+), Moderate (40%+) or High (60%+) risk for given dates. We matched all archived polygons for heavy precipitation (2,439 issuances, Dec 2017 - Oct 2026), heavy snow (1,921) and much below normal temperature (744 with polygons, Aug 2019 - Oct 2026) to CPC Unified gauge analyses on CONUS land cells. We wrote the plan before matching. The product does not say if a risk applies at least once in the valid dates or on each day. Heavy precipitation (3-day total above max(1 inch, 85th percentile)) was calibrated as an at-least-once probability: Slight 0.40 (95% CI 0.38-0.42), Moderate 0.49 (0.43-0.53), High 0.60 (0.45-0.74). Per 3-day window, Moderate (0.29) and High (0.37) were too high. Cold minima (below the 15th percentile and at most 2 C) were calibrated per day (0.30, 0.50, 0.74), but as at-least-once probabilities Slight (0.59) and Moderate (0.72) were too low; this did not depend on the freezing value. A liquid-only snow upper bound was below the Slight and Moderate floors per window (0.14, 0.28). Inside each level, observed frequency followed the 1991-2020 same-date frequency of the event: Slight rain areas verified at 0.12 where that base rate was below 0.1 and at 0.51 where it was 0.3 or more; West 0.26, East 0.45. A logistic slope on the base rate was 0.75 (0.68-0.84) for rain and 0.85 (0.71-1.00) for cold, against 0 implied by the labels. In leave-one-year-out tests inside polygons, a level-plus-base-rate relabelling raised the Brier skill score against climatology from -0.02 (stated midpoints) to +0.10 for rain and from +0.12 to +0.39 for cold. Limitations: 0.25-0.5 degree gauge grids smooth point extremes; Tmax, heat and wind layers were not tested; the per-day rules and the relabelling model were added after first results; intervals use month blocks.

display.caption: Observed frequency per risk level for three CPC Week-2 hazards under two event rules (filled: at least once in the valid dates; open: per day or per 3-day window). Grey boxes: stated ranges. Dashed: 1991-2020 same-date climatology. Bars: 95% month-block bootstrap intervals.

Observed frequency inside polygons against the climatological frequency of the same event at the same cells and dates. Each level follows the base rate, so dry-climate cells verify below and wet-climate cells above the stated range.
Leave-one-year-out reliability for heavy precipitation inside polygons: stated midpoints, climatology, and a level-plus-base-rate logistic relabelling.
